title: Screen lock covers every desktop tool, What Ember did names the policy, macOS names fold, quoted formulas, and the first marked screenshot on Windows
owns: app/main/main.ts (tool gating, shared hunks), app/renderer/home/copy.ts (activity words), app/main/policy/policy.ts and vocabulary.ts, app/main/perception/**

items.title: Screen-lock gate (#81) misses describe_screen, open_app and change_setting: Ember still reads and acts on this computer's desktop while it is locked
items.scenario: The user asks "what's on my screen?" (or starts a task that runs a command and then opens an app) and presses Win+L or Super+L, or the screen locks on idle, while the turn is still running. LockController only cancels tasks that have already used the desktop, so the conversation turn and a commands-only task keep going. (1) The model calls describe_screen. host.ts describeTarget gets null from targets.describeScreen('local') and calls this.o.describeScreen(). main.ts:1758 wires that to `seeing.describe()`, where `seeing` is the raw Perception (main.ts:1560), not the lockedOutHands-wrapped hands.perception. Perception.describe() reads the focused window and the open windows through accessibility and sends the text to the model while the screen is locked. (2) The task calls open_app. worker.ts:1144 calls perception.windows(): the gate refuses it and the error is caught to []. Then worker.ts:1152 calls `await apps.launch(app)` with no lock check, and Firefox starts on the locked desktop. The policy allows it as reversible (policy.ts:2195), so nobody is asked. change_setting (worker.ts:1101, sys.settings.change) also changes a desktop setting unasked. docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §4.4 promises that while the screen is locked Ember 'doesn't read or act on this computer's screen'.
items.evidence: Read main.ts:1560 and 1758, host.ts:1438-1446 (describeTarget), screen-lock.ts:290-317 (lockedOutHands gates only hands.perception, hands.sidecar and currentWindow), targets/hands.ts:80-90 (screenHands marks apps.launch as a use but doesn't gate it), worker.ts:1136-1160 and 1100-1102. Scratch test /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/perc/lock-gate.test.ts passes (run with --config vitest.config.mts in that folder). With the screen locked, lockedOutHands(h).perception.describe() rejects, screenHands(lockedOutHands(h)).system.apps.launch(Firefox) still calls the launcher, and main.ts's describeScreen is `seeing.describe()` on the raw Perception.
items.cause: fix/voice (#81, round 2) put the lock gate only on Hands (perception, sidecar, currentWindow). AgentHost's describeScreen option (main.ts) and the WorkerSystem's apps.launch and settings.change, which come through targets/hands.ts screenHands, go around it.
items.fix: In main.ts pass `describeScreen: () => (screenLock?.locked ? Promise.resolve("This computer's screen is locked, so Ember didn't read it.") : seeing.describe())`, or route it through hands.perception.describe(). In screenHands, or in a lock-aware WorkerSystem wrapper next to lockedOutHands, make system.apps.launch and system.settings.change reject with LOCKED_SCREEN while screenLock.locked. Add a check in the worker's open_app after windows() as a backstop.
items.skeptic:
I confirmed the finding. It is a real but low-impact gap in the #81 fix.

**1. describe_screen reads the screen while it is locked.**
- main.ts:1560 sets `const seeing = perception` (the raw Perception), and main.ts:1758 passes `describeScreen: () => seeing.describe()`.
- lockedOutHands (screen-lock.ts:290-317) wraps only the `hands` object and never touches this option.
- For local and WSL targets, host.ts:1442-1444 (describeTarget) gets null from runtime.ts:1553 describeScreen and falls through to `this.o.describeScreen()`.
- Perception.describe (perception/index.ts:389) has no lock check.
- Nothing ends a turn that is already running when the screen locks. askEmber refuses only new requests (main.ts:898). LockController only cancels local tasks that used the desktop (host.ts:1626). VoiceService.setLocked (voice.ts:200) only stops listening and speech.
- So a turn that calls describe_screen after the lock reads the focused window and the window list and sends them to the model.

**2. open_app and change_setting act while the screen is locked.**
- screenHands (targets/hands.ts:89) wraps `system.apps.launch` only to mark it as a desktop use. It is never gated.
- worker.ts:1144 catches the refused `windows()` call as an empty list, and 1152 calls `apps.launch` anyway.
- policy.ts:2195 allows open_app and setting as "reversible", so nobody is asked.
- I ran a scratch test: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/perc-skeptic/worker-lock.test.ts (run with that folder's vitest.config.mts). It builds a real Worker on `screenHands(lockedOutHands(h, () => locked))` with a real PolicyEngine, then sets `locked = true`:
  - open_app("firefox") called the launcher once. The raw perception's windows() was never reached, because the gate worked.
  - change_setting(dark_mode, on) called `settings.change` once.
  - Both were audited `verdict: "allow"`, reason "easy to undo", with no question asked.
- change_setting doesn't even count as a desktop use, so the 2-s sweep would never stop a task that only changes settings.
- Remote computers refuse this case on their own side ("build-01's desktop isn't ready: \"locked\"", per worker-commands.test.ts). So this is a gap only on this computer.

**Why it isn't refuted.**
- No guard elsewhere covers these paths.
- docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 accepts no such limitation.
- §4.4 explicitly promises Ember "doesn't read or act on this computer's screen" while it is locked.
- Neither lead-notes "Open interaction notes" nor "Follow-ups after merge" lists it.
- The voice report marks #81 fixed and names only the idle fallback poll and WSL commands as not done.

**Severity: minor or lower.** Nothing reaches a person at the locked computer: the lock screen covers the bubble and any app that opens, and maySpeak is false. The model only gets the screen text the user just asked about. Any app opened or setting changed is one the user asked for, and it is reversible. Both cases need the lock to land while a turn or task is already running. What breaks is the documented promise and parity with remote computers, not security.

items.title: 'What Ember did' records the policy watch's stop as 'Everything stopped (menu)'
items.scenario: While Ember runs, the administrator changes /etc/ember/policy.json (or the HKLM PolicyJson value, or the macOS file). The watch confirms the change, and main.ts:1901 calls killSwitch.pull("policy"), which writes audit {event:"stop", source:"policy"}. In Settings > What Ember did, describeEntry maps every source that isn't hotkey, voice or settings to "menu", so the timeline shows 'Stopped — Everything stopped (menu)'. That tells the user they stopped Ember from the handle's menu, when their organisation's policy change stopped it.
items.evidence: Scratch test /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/perc/stop-source.test.ts: describeEntry({event:'stop', source:'policy'}) returns what = 'Everything stopped (menu)' (the assertion that it doesn't say 'menu' fails). git log -L on copy.ts:471 shows the 'settings' branch came from fix/ask (229d55f). StopSource 'policy' came from fix/policy (#112, killswitch.ts:21).
items.cause: fix/policy (#112) added StopSource "policy". fix/ask then extended the activity wording for "settings" on its own branch, without "policy", and the merge kept the fallback to "menu".
items.fix: In describeEntry's 'stop' case, add `e.source === "policy" ? "your organisation changed Ember's policy"` before the "menu" fallback, or word the whole line differently, e.g. 'Everything stopped: your organisation changed Ember's policy'. Add a copy test for the policy source.
items.skeptic: I confirmed the finding. In the merged tree, killswitch.ts:21 includes "policy" in StopSource. main.ts:1901 calls killSwitch.pull("policy") when watchAdminPolicy confirms a change. pull() writes the audit entry {event:"stop", source:"policy"} (killswitch.ts:45) through `() => audit`, and nothing sets audit back to null after the policy hold. IPC.activity (main.ts:444) returns audit.recent(500) unfiltered, and renderer/home/main.ts:441 passes every entry to describeEntry. describeEntry's stop case (copy.ts:471) only has branches for hotkey, voice and settings, so everything else falls back to "menu". I ran the scratch test /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/perc/stop-source.test.ts against /home/user/wt/relfix-int. It fails with "expected 'Everything stopped (menu)' not to contain 'menu'". No audit entry for the policy change sits next to it and explains the stop (grep finds no policy or admin audit event in app/main). The lead-notes open items and follow-ups do not mention it. The policy report adds 'policy' to StopSource but has no matching copy change. The ask report only added "settings". At 63b88cd there was no policy watch, so this is an incomplete fix: fix/policy added a new stop source and nothing words it, not a regression. Minor severity is right: the safety behaviour is correct and only the timeline wording misattributes the stop. Related: app/remote/serve.ts:492 maps the remote agent's own "policy" stop to "menu" the same way (`source === "console" ? "remote-console" : "menu"`), so the remote's audit records it as a menu stop too.

items.title: macOS: Apple's German name for System Settings contains a soft hyphen, and the policy's Settings-app, security-app and never-look checks compare names without removing it, so they don't match on a German Mac
items.scenario: A German Mac. kCGWindowOwnerName is the app's localized name, and the darwin AX provider passes it on unchanged as the window's `app` (ax-darwin.ts:148/320 `app: owner`). For System Settings that name is "System­einstellungen". PolicyEngine checks `SETTINGS_APP[os]?.test(r.app.trim())` (policy.ts:1957), and the pattern is built with exactly([... "systemeinstellungen" ...]) in vocabulary.ts:95, which accepts no U+00AD. So systemSettings is false and the rule "every setting changed there is asked about" (policy.ts:1998/2006/2010/2043) is skipped. Once the user has granted "Always in this app", Ember can toggle switches in German System Settings (screen lock, login items and so on) without asking. isSecurityWindow (policy.ts:422) has the same gap for any SECURITY_APP name that Apple writes with U+00AD. isNeverLook (perception/elements.ts:460) has it too: a user who adds "Systemeinstellungen" to the never-look list doesn't keep Ember out, because the haystack holds "system­einstellungen". Commit 0d2717a folds \p{Cf} only inside the macOS app catalogue (apps.ts fold and appKey), not here.
items.evidence: ci.yml run 40801909158, macOS job, darwin-system "German names": the bundle's programs dump shows the bytes `s y s t e m 302 255 e i n s t e l l u n g e n`, U+00AD read from System Settings.app's InfoPlist.loctable. A scratch probe bundled from the merged sources (scratchpad/xreview/ship/shy/settings-app.ts) gives SETTINGS_APP.darwin.test("Systemeinstellungen")=true but test("System­einstellungen")=false; SECURITY_APP.darwin with soft hyphens is false; isSecurityWindow({app:"Schlüssel­bund­verwaltung"},"darwin") is false. The lead's own new unit case (darwin-system-apps.test.ts, 0d2717a) says "The window list may report the owner name with it or without it." What only a German Mac can prove is that kCGWindowOwnerName carries the U+00AD verbatim. That is the usual behaviour (the owner name is the localized bundle name), but I could not confirm it externally.
items.cause: policy package (SETTINGS_APP added in abab066 and the international SECURITY_APP names) together with platform #239 (localized macOS names) and the lead's 0d2717a, which normalizes only the catalogue
items.fix: Remove \p{Cf} (U+00AD included) from window owner names at the source: in the darwin window list/desktop entries (cg.ts owner), so the AX provider's `app`, wmClass, SECURITY_OWNERS checks and the catalogue all see one form. Alternatively, apply the same fold in isSecurityWindow, the SETTINGS_APP test and isNeverLook (both sides). Add a unit case: SETTINGS_APP/isSecurityWindow/isNeverLook with "System­einstellungen" must match.
items.skeptic:
I couldn't refute the main System Settings claim. I ran it end to end on the merged code. Two caveats lower the severity.

1. The code path holds and nothing normalizes the name along the way.
   - ax-darwin.ts:148 and :320 pass kCGWindowOwnerName through as `app` (cg.ts:44 and ax-darwin-api.ts:398 copy it unchanged).
   - The worker sends `this.window.app` into the policy request.
   - policy.ts:1957 tests `SETTINGS_APP[os]?.test(r.app.trim())` against `exactly([... "systemeinstellungen" ...])` (vocabulary.ts:30/95). Nothing there removes \p{Cf}.
   - The only places that fold \p{Cf} are apps.ts `fold` (0d2717a, catalogue and appKey only), elements.ts `normalize` (labels), `quotable` and the policy's INVISIBLE set. None of them touch `r.app`, isSecurityWindow (policy.ts:421) or isNeverLook (elements.ts:460).
   - Grants are keyed by `req.app.toLowerCase()` (worker.ts:3408, policy.ts:2197). So an "Always" saved for "system­einstellungen" is found again every time, and nothing re-routes the check.

2. I ran it. The probe is scratchpad/xreview/ship/shy2/e2e.ts, bundled with esbuild, using the real PolicyEngine on darwin with a grant.
   - toggle(app "Systemeinstellungen", window "Kamera", switch "Terminal") gives confirm/risky ("this changes a system setting...").
   - The same request with app "System­einstellungen" gives verdict allow, tier reversible ("Ember may act in System­einstellungen").
   - "Anmeldeobjekte" (login items) behaves the same way.
   - The Sperrbildschirm switch "Passwort nach Ruhezustand verlangen" is still asked, but only because securitySetting matches its label ("Passwort"), not because of SETTINGS_APP.
   - Never-look: with "Systemeinstellungen" on the list, a read in "System­einstellungen" is allowed and isNeverLook returns false.
   - No other guard covers these windows: the darwin never-look defaults hold no Settings entry, and SECURITY_TITLE only names "Datenschutz & Sicherheit", not "Kamera" or "Anmeldeobjekte".

3. The premise about the name is strongly supported, though only a German Mac can confirm it.
   - The CI dump (mac141.log:14) shows the German entry of System Settings' InfoPlist.loctable has CFBundleName "system­einstellungen" and no CFBundleDisplayName. So the localized bundle name carries U+00AD.
   - An external report (OpenWhispr PR #2294, commit ea7f11a) says kCGWindowOwnerName "is the localized bundle name", which is "Systemeinstellungen" on a German Mac.
   - The lead's own test in 0d2717a allows that the window list may report either spelling.
   - Nothing points to the WindowServer stripping \p{Cf}.

4. It isn't covered elsewhere. It's not in the lead-notes open items or follow-ups, and not in COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26.

Caveats that lower severity:
- (a) It isn't a regression against 63b88cd. SETTINGS_APP is new in abab066 (review #111), so on a German Mac the merged code behaves as the base did. It's an incomplete fix, though abab066's own test names German "Systemeinstellungen" as a target.
- (b) It only bites after an "Always in System Settings" grant, or an "Allow" earlier in the same task, for switches whose labels don't say security.
- (c) The isSecurityWindow/Keychain part is speculation. The finding gives no evidence that Apple writes "Schlüsselbundverwaltung" with soft hyphens, and the English "keychain access" never-look default and SECURITY_APP entries are unaffected.
- (d) The never-look miss is pre-existing behaviour, and only applies when the user types the German name.

Net: confirmed, but it's closer to moderate than major. The fix stands: remove \p{Cf} from the darwin owner name at the source, or apply apps.ts `fold` in the SETTINGS_APP test, isSecurityWindow and isNeverLook.

items.text: policy #116 (partial): the approval card shows apostrophes in place of a formula's real double quotes (typing =IF(A1="x";1;0) shows =IF(A1='x';1;0)), so the user approves text that isn't what will be typed. Show typed text faithfully, real ASCII double quotes included, while still keeping look-alike quotes and line breaks from making typed text pass for Ember's own words (e.g. quote typed text in a clearly delimited block whose delimiter the text can't contain or close, and mark look-alikes). policy's note: Round 1: quote() turns double-quote look-alikes into apostrophes, line breaks into spaces, and drops format characters. Typed text shows whole up to 160 characters; longer text shows its first 110 and last 40 characters and its length. Round 2: the 'value' question quotes the value with quote(r.value, 40), with an ellipsis when cut, so 'Set “Brightness” slider to “50 in Firefox? Nothing is sent. Delete…”' can't pass for Ember's own words. Decision.detail now carries the whole cleaned typed text whenever the question cut it. Left for the bubble and agent packages: show Decision.detail on the card, expandable (see notes).

Windows (and any OS where it applies): the first screenshot with Ember's marks on a fresh machine pays fontconfig's cache build, because the marks are SVG text drawn by sharp (CI measured 2 s on one runner and more than 15 s on another; the cache is on disk, per user, so it is paid once). Warm sharp's text rendering in the background a few seconds after start, off the main thread, best effort, without delaying start-up or the first read; never on a machine where it isn't needed more than once (sharp's work after the cache exists is milliseconds). Test that it is scheduled once, is best effort, and doesn't run when Ember starts for --doctor.
